sections.heading: Core Concepts
sections.content: The factorial (n!) is the classic first problem for learning **recursion**. n! equals n times (n-1)!, shrinking the problem each step until the simplest case is reached.
items: **Base Case**: 0! = 1 (or 1! = 1) is the [[primary|stopping condition]] of the recursion
**Recurrence**: n! = n × (n-1)! hands the larger problem to a smaller one of the same kind
Each call pushes a new frame onto the **call stack**, holding the current n
After the Base Case, results are **returned** and multiplied layer by layer

sections.heading: Operation Complexity
sections.content: There are n levels of recursion, each doing one multiplication, but every level keeps a stack frame alive.
items: **Space complexity**: [[warning|O(n)]] — the call stack grows to n frames
Rewriting it as a **loop** reduces space to [[success|O(1)]]

sections.heading: Things to Watch
sections.content: Factorials grow extremely fast, so mind both recursion depth and numeric range.
items: **A missing Base Case** causes infinite recursion and eventually a **stack overflow**
Even modest n exceeds fixed-width integers; consider **big-number arithmetic**
The recursive version is mainly valuable for **understanding the call stack**; loops are preferred in practice
